first_impression.reaction: Not the kind of thing I'd normally search, but my fiancee asked what the sixpence is about. The intro tells me straight away what's covered, and the takeaways give me a year (1883) instead of 'ancient tradition' waffle. FAQ first as usual: short, plain answers. Then I jumped to the insurance section, because that's where real money is, and skimmed the rest.

journey.quote: The rhyme was first recorded in 1883, as the saying of "some Lancashire friends", and the sixpence line appears in print with it by 1946.
journey.reaction: Dates, not mythology. Most wedding sites would tell me it goes back to the Romans or something. This I can actually check.

journey.quote: In the left shoe. Many couples tape it inside the shoe or tuck it under the insole so it is comfortable all day.
journey.reaction: Answered in one line, plus a practical tip. That's all I wanted from the FAQ.

journey.section: 3. Something old: heirlooms with a story
journey.quote: Have a jeweller check clasps and settings a few months before the wedding, so nothing gives way on the day.
journey.reaction: Practical, and nobody's trying to sell me the jeweller. Fine.

journey.section: 8. Modern and luxury ways to do all four
journey.quote: These are the combinations we see work best:
journey.reaction: 'We see work best' based on what, how many weddings? It's a list of ideas, which is fine, but don't dress it up as track record. Minor.

journey.section: 9. Carrying heirlooms to a destination wedding
journey.quote: Standard travel insurance policies typically don't cover items stolen from checked baggage on an airline, train or bus.
journey.reaction: This is the catch I'd want flagged before a family ring goes overseas. Most useful line on the page for me.

journey.section: 9. Carrying heirlooms to a destination wedding
journey.quote: Credit card travel insurance may only cover the cardholder, and generally only the trip paid for on the card.
journey.reaction: Another fine-print trap, called out plainly. They're telling me where policies bite instead of pretending it's all covered.

journey.section: 9. Carrying heirlooms to a destination wedding
journey.quote: A borrowed piece belongs to someone else, so ask the owner whether their own contents policy covers it overseas before it leaves home.
journey.reaction: Hadn't thought of that. Good. Saves an awkward conversation with my future mother-in-law.

journey.section: 9. Carrying heirlooms to a destination wedding
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments around the day, as your single point of contact.
journey.reaction: 'Payments' is where my ears prick up. If the money flows through you, do you take a cut from the venue and vendors? Comes after the useful stuff at least.

journey.quote: When you are ready to talk through where to marry and how to bring your family pieces with you, tell us your date, your guest list and the feeling you want.
journey.reaction: 'The feeling you want' is soft. Tell me what the first call covers and whether it costs anything.

journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and your advisor confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Fee in writing up front is the right signal. Still doesn't say how the fee is worked out or whether there are supplier commissions on top.

unanswered_questions: Does Wedded Wonderland take commissions or mark-ups from venues, vendors or hotels, especially if payments go through the Wedded Advisor?
What does the Wedded Advisor fee cover and how is it calculated?
Is the first call with a Wedded Advisor free, and what does it cover?
Is there a real wedding example with the actual budget?

turn_offs_found.quote: These are the combinations we see work best:
turn_offs_found.why: Implied track record with nothing behind it. Minor; the list itself is useful.

turn_offs_found.quote: tell us your date, your guest list and the feeling you want.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional sales phrasing where I'd rather know what happens next. Minor.

would_share_with: My fiancee, for the sixpence and something borrowed sections
Her mother, for the carrying-heirlooms and insurance checklist before any family piece flies

cta_reaction.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and your advisor confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
cta_reaction.why: The CTA comes after the evidence and the written-fee line is what I look for. But a blog post about a rhyme isn't going to make me enquire; I'd go looking for a fees or commissions page first.

top_3_changes: In the closing section, swap 'the feeling you want' for what the first call covers and whether it's free.
Soften or ground 'These are the combinations we see work best' (e.g. 'Combinations that work well'), so it doesn't read as an unbacked track-record claim. Minor.
Say, even in one line, whether the Wedded Advisor takes commissions or mark-ups from suppliers (business detail deferred, so nice-to-have).

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ first, looked for dates, catches, fee model, commissions
No invented brand facts; missing fee, commission and first-call details placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments ignored
Title (person-set) and deferred business details not flagged as must-fix; no requests for sourcing or documentation lines, per orchestrator

open_questions.question: Is a fees or how-we-charge page available to link from the CTA? Business details are deferred, so treat as nice-to-have.

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'something old something new' after his fiancee asked about the tradition; low relevance reflects topic fit for a sceptical groom, not a draft fault.
No prices on the page is the house standard and not penalised.
